content:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for ingest-service v2.3.1 → 15% traffic (region: us-west1). config: feature_flag=new_user_idx=true, db-migration=20260712_add_user_idx.sql :rocket:

sara: noticed a spike in 500s in the canary within ~3 minutes. errors look like SQL constraint violations. quick glance from the dashboard: p50 latency +180ms, errors ~6% of canary requests. tagging db-oncall. :eyes:

pagerduty: Incident triggered - Escalating to on-call: mike (db-oncall). PagerDuty incident: PD-98765 :rotating_light:

mike: on it. can anyone paste the exact error from logs?

sara: grabbing logs, here's a tail from the app pod: 
```
ERROR: insert or update on table "users" violates not-null constraint
DETAIL: Key (email)=(null) violates not-null constraint "users_email_not_null"
org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: ERROR: null value in column "email" violates not-null constraint
```

jenn: that migration was supposed to add an index and backfill emails for imported users. it included a small backfill job but it was gated by a new code path that didn't fill email for oauth-only signups.

mike: ok. looks like the code started writing rows without email before the backfill completed. canary traffic is hitting those codepaths. two immediate options: 1) flip feature flag new_user_idx=false to stop the code path; 2) kill canary and rollback the service deploy. flipping flag is lower blast radius.

lucas: agree with flag flip first. I can toggle in Console. prepping command: 
```
# feature-gate toggle
redwood feature-flags set new_user_idx false --env=prod --region=us-west1
```

sara: doing the toggle now. flipping to false...

ops-bot: Feature flag "new_user_idx" set to false by sara at 2026-07-12T00:16:12Z :white_check_mark:

sara: immediate drop in 500s to ~0.5% in the canary. latency back to baseline. :thumbsup:

mike: good mitigation. next we need to ensure DB is consistent before resuming. the migration 20260712_add_user_idx.sql failed halfway on some partitions. we should NOT re-run it blindly. can someone run a selective validation query to count NULL emails introduced since deploy?

jenn: running query: 
```
SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE email IS NULL AND created_at > '2026-07-12T00:00:00Z';
```

jenn: result: 1,242 rows (canary + small percentage from background jobs).

mike: thanks. plan: 1) keep feature flag off; 2) patch service to reject writes that would create null email (safest short-term), or better: ensure code supplies placeholder email for oauth flows; 3) run a conservative backfill to set placeholder emails for affected rows OR run targeted manual corrections; 4) once backfill validated, roll migration forward with a SHORT windowed backfill and monitor.

lucas: i'll open a quick PR that sets placeholder for missing emails in the oauth flow and cut a hotfix canary on a 5% rollout. we want to avoid reintroducing the bad behavior. estimated PR + canary: 35 minutes.

mike: meanwhile i'll coordinate with infra to snapshot the user table partition and take a backup in case we need to revert changes. also asking SRE to hold off on promoting canary until we confirm backfill.

ops-bot: Backup job started: snapshot users_partition_2026_07_12 by ops @ 2026-07-12T00:28:03Z :floppy_disk:

sara: customer impact check: ops dashboards show ~1200 requests failed (5xx) affecting ~350 unique customer API keys during the ~3m window. tentative severity: sev2. i'm drafting a short status page update.

mike: good. whoever picks this up for the next shift, here's the concrete runbook we used: 
- flip feature flag new_user_idx=false (done)
- take DB snapshot (done)
- patch code to not emit null emails (PR link: https://git.redwood/intern/ingest/pulls/432)
- run targeted backfill: 
```
UPDATE users SET email = concat('missing+', id, '@placeholder.redwood') WHERE email IS NULL AND created_at >= '2026-07-12T00:00:00Z';
```
- validate no regressions for 30m in canary; then slowly resume rollout

jenn: backfill run in dry mode first (SELECT to preview) - looks safe. will run UPDATE after PR merges and hotfix is verified.

sara: communicating to ops and to the customer success team: short note pushed to #customer-ops. draft message: 
"We observed intermittent 500s for ingest API in us-west1 during a canary rollout. We rolled back the feature flag and are applying a fix. Estimated ETA for full resume: ~90 minutes. If you saw missing emails in your imports, contact support."

lucas: PR merged, hotfix canary started at 00:58 UTC to 5%. logs show no null-email writes so far.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: hotfix canary for ingest-service v2.3.1-hotfix started (5%)

mike: plan for next 60–90 mins: run the non-destructive backfill, monitor error rates and customer tickets. if anything spikes, we rollback migrations and cut an emergency release to revert code change that expects the migration.

sara: handing off to night on-call lucas for monitoring and runbook follow-through. lucas, please escalate to infra if snapshot restores are needed.

lucas: taking over. checklist acknowledged. i'll post updates every 30m and close with postmortem stub.

pagerduty: Incident PD-98765 updated: severity downgraded to SEV2 -> monitoring. assigned to lucas.

sara: final note before handoff - triggers for postmortem: why did migration/backfill order allow writes that would violate constraints? action items: (A) adjust deployment gating to require backfill completion before code that depends on it, (B) improve deploy-runbook to include a preflight check for nullability regressions, (C) add a schema-change simulator to our staging tests.

lucas: added to incident ticket. will produce a short postmortem by EOD tomorrow with timeline and RCA. closing on-call thread here, will reopen if anything regresses. :lock:

sara: thanks all. great run-through.

-- end thread --
